name: develop-like-sudipta
description: v5.0.6 fixes 4 field-reported bugs from a live /cc-drive session (2026-07-31, Django multi-tenant repo, Path A). BUG-1 P0 `send.sh` — `set -euo pipefail` + the FRAG picker's `grep -oE '[!-~ ]{15,200}'` meant ANY message without a 15-char printable-ASCII run (`/clear`, `/compact`, `yes`, `2`) killed the script silently BEFORE pbcopy/osascript ran: exit 1, zero output, no log, no state event, manager believed the send landed. Fixed with `{ grep ... || true; }` so the existing fallback becomes reachable; added an EXIT trap that logs `[send] ABORT rc=N at line N` to stderr + `send.log` so the script can never again die silently; PLUS BUG-1b found during verification — screen-mutating commands (`/clear` wipes scrollback, `/compact` replaces it) destroyed the very evidence verify-by-fragment polls for, so a SUCCESSFUL send reported FAIL exit 2; now case-matched and verified by the inverse assertion (command must NOT still sit at the prompt). New `test_send_short_messages.sh` extracts the FRAG picker from the real send.sh via awk range (cannot drift) and asserts 9 contracts — RED 8/9 before, GREEN 9/9 after; live-verified `/clear` exits 0. BUG-2 P1 watchdog — Django's `DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS test_app_master` tripped base danger pattern 46 five times in one session and the only escape hatch (danger_patterns_extra.txt) can only ADD patterns; repeatedly approving DROP DATABASE by reflex is the opposite of a deny-list's purpose. New project-scoped ALLOW-list at `<ws>/.cc/danger_patterns_allow.txt`, checked BEFORE the deny scan; match → skip deny, log `ALLOW fp=...` loudly, emit `danger_exempted` state event + learning event. Ships `assets/danger_patterns_allow.example.txt` with THE ONE RULE (an exemption must be narrower than the pattern it exempts) and three commented Django/pytest examples. New `test_danger_allow_list.sh` proves 4 contracts: allow-match exempted, same-pattern real-DB still refused, no-file back-compat refusal, comment-only-file refusal. BUG-3 P2 cc-drive.md — terminal autocomplete ghost suggestions render byte-identically to typed input in read.sh output; the single-read heuristic logged phantom `user_direct_input` events 5 times in one session. Doc fix (no styling signal exists in plain text): require BOTH same-text-across-two-polls-≥30s AND submission evidence; ghost suggestions persist unchanged and are never submitted; acting on a phantom instruction is worse than missing a real one. Retraction pattern (`user_direct_input_retracted`) documented in failure_modes.md. BUG-4 P3 audit.sh — files-changed section dumped 40+ paths uncapped, burying the Mentioned-but-NOT-changed signal; display now capped at 20 + `(N more)` tail, full list still feeds the miss-check so exit-code semantics unchanged. Eval suite 39 → 41. v5.0.5 ships 10 deploy-hardening fixes from a real-world field report (GuardianAI 20-phase greenfield build on a NUC target — full report archived in commit thread). Three commits + 3 new RED→GREEN regression evals (suite 36 → 39). (FAILURE 4) watchdog detects CC's `Interrupted ·` UI state distinct from permission prompts, emits a `prompt_interrupted` state event with NO keystroke; manager responds via send.sh with a typed re-trigger. New `test_watchdog_interrupt_detection.sh` asserts the event lands + no key pressed. (FAILURE 10) new `scripts/skip_nudge_patterns.txt` with 25 long-I/O substrings (docker pull/build, npm/pip/cargo install, Pulling from, Downloading from, …); `nudge_if_stuck.sh` scans the last 20 buffer lines via `grep -F` before pressing Esc on a confirmed hang, emits `nudge_skipped` event on match; per-workspace `<ws>/.cc/skip_nudge_patterns_extra.txt` picked up dynamically. `install.sh` wires the new file via a DATA_FILES array; also belatedly adds `unblock_cc.sh` to SCRIPTS (v5.0.2 oversight). New `test_nudge_skip_patterns.sh` proves three contracts (suppress on match, fire on genuine hang, extras file picked up). (FAILURES 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9) SKILL.md adds `## Known footguns` with: env-load via `set -a && source .env && set +a` (xargs silently fails on URLs / special chars), parallel-SSH+CC build conflict warning, interrupt-recovery contract, skip-nudge mechanism. `assets/directive_template.md` adds an `## (Optional) Deploy phase template` block with: docker base-image cache preflight (2-min timeout fallback), `ss -tlnp` + `docker ps` port-conflict preflight, env-load with API_PORT assertion, Option A docker / Option B direct-venv ladder, OLLAMA_MODEL + OLLAMA_MODEL_FALLBACK rate-limit retry pattern, tmux multi-window layout, MANDATORY `curl /health 200` acceptance with explicit 'Do not mark phase_complete without a 200 from /health' prose. New `test_deploy_directive_template.sh` grep-asserts 14 required phrases — any future text drift trips the eval. v5.0.4 (May 2026 drift sweep) closes three drift surfaces with 6 commits + 2 new regression-guard evals (suite 34 → 36). Phase 1 fixed three documented gaps: CLAUDE.md's stale `5.0.1` version reference (now `5.0.3`); `ccbridge_status.sh`'s EXPECTED_SCRIPTS list missing `unblock_cc.sh` (the v5.0.2 BUG-4 helper was already deployed via install.sh but the health-check reported 'red — 1 problem(s) detected' against a fully healthy install); and `commands/cc-resume.md` lacking a pointer to the v5.0.3 no-sleep continuous-manager doctrine — a resumed session might have fallen back to old poll-and-return patterns without the inline pointer + 3-end-of-turn-condition reminder (job_complete, monitor.stop, 3 consecutive failed unblock attempts). Phase 2 added `test_precommit_hooks_dir_coverage.sh` as a regression guard on the pre-commit `/Users/<name>/` scanner — directive predicted RED ('hooks/scripts/ is a blind spot') but empirically the hook ALREADY covers hooks/scripts/ via the `develop-like-sudipta/hooks` SHIP_DIRS entry + nested-prefix matching in `is_in_ship_dir`. The predicted bug-driven-TDD red→fix sequence didn't materialize; the eval ships anyway with positive (synthetic offender at hooks/scripts/test_helper_TEMP.sh → hook refuses with the canonical 'HARDCODED PATH(S) DETECTED' message) + negative (hardcoded path inside an EXEMPT_PATHS entry → no refusal so the hook doesn't self-flag) assertions to catch future SHIP_DIRS narrowing. Phase 3 added `test_bash3_2_compat.sh`, a Python-driven scan that walks every bridge + hook script for bash 4+ features (`declare -A`, `${var,,}` / `${var^^}`, `mapfile` / `readarray`, `coproc`, `${var@Q}` / `${var@a}`, `wait -t`) with comment-line + heredoc-body filtering; all 37 scripts are bash 3.2 clean including the v5.0.x additions (sync_learnings.sh, propose_fix_pr.sh, dispatch_signature.sh, escalate.sh, nudge_if_stuck.sh, ccbridge_status.sh, unblock_cc.sh). Detection itself was sanity-verified against a synthetic offender file containing all four representative bash 4+ constructs — audit caught each on its own line with the right feature name. Three drift gaps closed empirically; two latent classes of regression now have automated guards. v5.0.3 codifies the manager no-sleep contract that emerged from the v5.0.2 stability run. New `## Continuous-manager doctrine` section in `skills/sd-claude-code-access/SKILL.md` and `commands/cc-drive.md`: once `<workspace>/.cc/active-job.json` exists, the manager (Cowork) never ends its turn until ONE of five conditions fires — `state.sh job_complete`, `done_criteria` satisfied, `<ws>/.cc/monitor.stop` file appears, user explicit stop, or 3 consecutive failed unblock attempts. Per-cycle (30-60s) actions documented inline: read CC buffer, fire `unblock_cc.sh` directly on `❯ N.` prompts (don't wait for the orchestrator's per-minute fire-gap), grep `git log` for new commits, send next-phase trigger manually via `send.sh` when `phase_complete N` lands and `phase-(N+1).md` exists. Parallel work the manager can do inside the turn (without pausing CC) explicitly enumerated: mid-run bug-driven TDD fixes, audit checkpoints, three-place SKILL refresh (assets/ → ~/Documents/Claude/Scheduled/ → MCP `update_scheduled_task`). Anti-patterns section grows two new bans: 'Don't end the turn while an active job exists' and 'Don't return to user while CC is actively working on a phase'. RED→GREEN regression eval `evals/test_no_sleep_doctrine.sh` grep-asserts 8 doctrine phrases in SKILL.md + cc-drive.md so any future text drift fails the eval suite. v5.0.2 (May 2026 stability hardening) closes the v5.0.x feedback loop with 12 commits across 6 phases (eval suite 24 → 33, coverage gate 71% → 91%). Phase 1 refreshed CLAUDE.md (4.4.0 → 5.0.1 version reference, 22 → 23 commands, 2 → 6 scheduled-task SKILLs, v5.0's `^claude$|/claude$` regex shape, eval-count claim) and backfilled `develop-like-sudipta/README.md`'s `## Versioning` section with 19 newest-first entries spanning v5.0.1 → v4.0.0 (previously skipped from v5.0.0 straight to v4.0.0). Phase 2 added two `cc-coordinator-keepalive` evals: the Step-1 idle quota-saver pins down the `find ~/Workspace -maxdepth 4 -name active-job.json` semantics (presence of `.cc/` is not enough — only the active-job marker triggers a per-fire cycle); the Step-2 stall-detection eval anchors the 7-min heartbeat threshold against macOS `date -u -j -f` parsing with positive (10m → STALLED), negative (1m → HEALTHY), and edge (exactly 7m → STALLED) cases. Phase 3 added a `cc-orchestrator` active-job eval covering three contracts: phase-advance branch (last event = `phase_complete` + next directive exists → send `Read .cc/phase-<N+1>.md and proceed.`), no-next-phase branch (`BLOCKED no-next-phase` learning event + pause), and the `.cc/monitor.stop` kill switch's highest-priority short-circuit (must beat the state-driven phase-advance branch when both fixtures coexist). Phase 4 is a documented skip — shellcheck wasn't installed on the dev Mac and the operating mode treated that as a legitimate completion (`state.json` records `skipped=shellcheck_absent`). Phase 5 introduced the script→eval coverage matrix gate at ≥80%: new `test_script_eval_coverage.sh` enumerates `scripts/` + `hooks/scripts/`, greps every `evals/test_*.sh` for basename references, and emits `SCRIPT_COVERAGE.md` as a snapshot side-effect; cleared the 80% gate via 3 new smoke evals — `lock.sh` (status/acquire/stale-recovery via dead-pid in `kill -0` check/held-by-live refusal with exit 2), `nudge_if_stuck.sh` (3-confirm Esc gate + `nudge_sent` state event under mocked `read.sh` + `keys.sh` + `state.sh`), and `ccbridge_status.sh` (green verdict over a synthetic CCBRIDGE_HOME with all 22 expected scripts + subdirs + projects.json; red verdict over an empty CCBRIDGE). Two scripts are allowlisted from the coverage denominator — `read_history.sh` (pure osascript wrapper mirroring `read.sh`) and `audit_danger_patterns.sh` (markdown report over `danger_patterns.txt` with semantics `test_danger_patterns.sh` already exercises). Three external bugs that landed mid-run: BUG-3 (`launch_cc.sh` defaulted `CC_LAUNCH_FLAGS` to `--continue --chrome --auto` but `claude 2.1.139` rejects `--auto` with `error: unknown option '--auto'` — the actual server-side L1 reviewer flag is `--permission-mode auto`; script now probes `claude --help` at launch and either includes the correct flag if `--permission-mode` is supported AND `auto` is one of its choices, or drops the flag entirely for graceful degradation), BUG-4 (`cc-orchestrator` cursor-position detection + new `unblock_cc.sh` helper that recovers stuck permission prompts when the manager's keystroke landed on the wrong menu option), and BUG-5/6 (`unblock_cc.sh` bounded logging + non-blocking `state.sh` dispatch to prevent hangs when state.sh itself is wedged). The `cc-orchestrator` + `cc-coordinator-keepalive` scheduled tasks ran the full 6-phase loop end-to-end on this stability run — the v5.0 L1/L2/L3 architecture self-validated as a side effect of the hardening it shipped. v5.0.1 patches BUG-2 — `watchdog.sh`'s `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM` cleaned up the DENY_SRC tmpfile on signal but did NOT exit the `while true` loop, so SIGTERM was effectively ignored and every wrapper (launch_cc, start_watchdog, evals) had to escalate to SIGKILL — which bypasses traps and also defeats the cleanup. Fix splits into two traps: EXIT runs cleanup only; INT/TERM run cleanup AND `exit 143` explicitly (128 + SIGTERM(15), conventional). New eval `evals/test_watchdog_sigterm_exits.sh` is the RED→GREEN regression: sends SIGTERM ONLY (no SIGKILL fallback inside assertion window), asserts the process exited within 5s. RED before fix (watchdog still alive after 5s → BUG-2 reproduced), GREEN after. Stale workaround comment in the sibling `test_watchdog_safety_net_only.sh` updated to note SIGKILL is now belt-and-suspenders rather than the only working option. All 23 evals remain green; no behavioral changes outside signal handling. v5.0.0 ships the continuous-loop architecture in three layers, backed by docs/plans/research-continuous-cowork-2026-05-12.md and landed in 35+ commits over 7 plan phases. L1 — launch_cc.sh now defaults CC_LAUNCH_FLAGS to '--continue --chrome --auto', routing every CC tool call through Anthropic's April-2026 Sonnet-4.6 server-side reviewer (per-call block on scope escalation / untrusted infra / prompt injection). L2 — new cc-orchestrator scheduled task (cron '* * * * *') is the per-minute reasoning watcher: reads <workspace>/.cc/active-job.json, polls CC's buffer via read.sh, decides approve/deny/revise via keys.sh + send.sh, advances phases on phase_complete events, escalates stalls. Step-1 early-exit when no active-job.json keeps idle machines quota-free. L3 — cc-coordinator-keepalive (cron '*/5 * * * *') is the watchdog over the orchestrator: detects heartbeat staleness > 7 min, fires Slack/email via mcp__02da* + mcp__da8a* when notify_* channels are set, self-disables both scheduled tasks via mcp__scheduled-tasks__update_scheduled_task enabled=false once every active job hits its done_criteria. Stop conditions are mandatory: max_cycles + max_duration_hours + <workspace>/.cc/monitor.stop kill switch + max_fix_attempts_per_cycle cooldown + cycle_timeout_s wall-clock cap. The active-watcher pivot also reshapes the v4.x watchdog: default is now WATCHDOG_AUTO_APPROVE=0 (safety-net only — refuses danger patterns, logs everything else as prompt_pending for the manager to attend); legacy auto-approve is opt-in for unattended scheduled-task runs. New skill reference references/active_watcher.md covers the manager-decides model, polling cadence, per-prompt decision tree, job-spec schema, stop conditions, escalation channels. New ## Modes section in the skill maps use cases to artifact patterns: Mode A greenfield phased build, Mode B SRE monitor, Mode C single hotfix. Cross-machine learnings sync (Phase 6): scripts/sync_learnings.sh rsyncs peer Macs' learning tails over passwordless SSH (per-peer best-effort, --update incremental, --dry-run preview), the new ccbridge-sync-learnings scheduled task (cron '0 */6 * * *') sweeps every 6 hours, aggregate_learnings.sh walks learnings/remote-*/*.jsonl with source_host tags, and distillation gains a cross-machine? dimension that weights cross-machine signatures strictly higher than single-machine cross-project (different hardware converging on the same pattern = stronger universal signal). Privacy: only per-workspace .jsonl tails travel (hashed ws_id, no raw paths); aggregated/, distillation/, and projects.json stay local-only. Six bundled scheduled tasks now: ccbridge-aggregate-learnings (nightly 02:15), ccbridge-distill-and-propose (Sundays 03:30), ccbridge-propose-fix-pr (Mondays 09:00), cc-orchestrator (every minute), cc-coordinator-keepalive (every 5 min), ccbridge-sync-learnings (every 6 hours). /ccbridge-init registers/refreshes all six idempotently, preserving user-customized crons. BUG-1 (launch_cc.sh detect filter missed bare-name 'claude' argv[0] — caused --detect-only to false-negative on user-shell-launched CCs) fixed via bug-driven TDD: red test → regex change to '$2 ~ /^claude$|\/claude$/' in launch_cc.sh + start_watchdog.sh → four greens; eval hardened for non-interactive runners via /usr/bin/script pty + compound bash body + pidfile capture. Also fixed: H4 diagnose.sh settings.local.json validity check (JSON parse + stray ':*' counter with pipefail-safe || echo 0) + D2/D3/D5 doc gaps (launch_cc --continue semantics on new workspaces, Chrome MCP coexistence rules, audit.sh manual-only trigger semantics). v4.8.0 closes the F-AUTOPR autonomy gap — when `ccbridge-distill-and-propose` (Sunday) surfaces a cross-project plugin signature (`CROSS_N >= 2`), the new `ccbridge-propose-fix-pr` scheduled task (Mondays 09:00 local) routes it through a portable dispatch table to the matching plugin file, spawns CC against the plugin repo clone via `~/.cache/ccbridge/launch_cc.sh`, drives a bug-driven TDD cycle (failing eval first, min fix, verify-gate green), and opens a **draft** PR via `gh pr create --draft --body-file <tmp>`. Maintainer reviews/merges — explicit-permission boundary preserved, no auto-merge. Capped at 3 PRs/week (`PR_CAP=3`); overflow batches into one GitHub issue rather than spamming N PRs. Bash 3.2-compatible case-statement dispatch lives in `scripts/dispatch_signature.sh` (testable in isolation), and the procedure runner `scripts/propose_fix_pr.sh` honors `DRY_RUN=1` (no PR-log writes, no `gh` calls — just narrate) and `GH_OVERRIDE=mock`. Three new evals enforce the contract: `test_propose_fix_pr_dispatch.sh` (13 known prefixes + 3 unknowns + empty-input rejection), `test_propose_fix_pr_dryrun.sh` (mktemp-isolated priors + PR log → asserts no side effects under DRY_RUN), `test_propose_fix_pr_cap.sh` (5 signatures → first 3 `WOULD spawn` + last 2 `batched_to_issue`). `install.sh` copies both new scripts into `~/.cache/ccbridge/` so the bundled SKILL.md can reference the stable per-machine paths (same pattern as `aggregate_learnings.sh` + `distill_learnings.sh` since v4.3.3). `/ccbridge-init` now registers/refreshes three scheduled tasks instead of two; `/ccbridge-status` reports on the third one too. v4.7.0 ships the first OBJECTIVE eval for watchdog prompt classification — caught 3 real plugin gaps during dogfooding on ProDevs-News (2026-05-11): (1) PROMPT_PATTERN missed 'Do you want to CREATE/write/edit/delete/run …' verbs (final C6 closure from earlier feedback — v4.6.0 fixed the broader 'Do you want to …' family but the verb list stayed incomplete), (2) numbered-menu form '❯ 1. Continue / 2. Fix / 3. Exit' (Settings Warning class) wasn't recognized — extended PROMPT_PATTERN with a '^❯ 1\. (Yes|Continue|Allow|Proceed)' alternation, (3) AWS/gcloud/azure cloud-storage recursive deletes weren't covered by danger_patterns.txt — added 5 new regexes for aws s3 rm --recursive, aws s3api delete-bucket/objects, gcloud storage rm --recursive, gsutil rm -r, az storage blob/container delete-batch. New eval at `skills/sd-claude-code-access/evals/watchdog_prompt_evals.json` (20 hand-labeled rows: 8 approve + 7 refuse + 5 ignore) + scorer `test_watchdog_prompts.sh` that shells out to actual `grep -qiE` for grep-faithful semantics. Baseline before fixes = 0.85 (3 misses), after fixes = 1.0000. Autoresearch-wirable — see WATCHDOG_PROMPTS_README.md for the autoresearch sub-loop wiring spec (v4.8 task). Existing `test_danger_patterns.sh` regression: still 45/45 destructive caught + 32/32 routine allowed (no false-positive introduced). Closes the F-EVALS proposal from plugin-feedback-v4.6.1-proposal-2026-05-11.md. v4.6.2 fills the critical Swarm-vs-Compose gap in v4.6.1's deploy policy — caught by dogfooding on ProDevs-News (2026-05-11): pull_policy: always works for plain docker-compose endpoints but is SILENTLY DROPPED by Docker Swarm. Stack file passes through with the directive intact (docker cp from portainer container shows it on disk) but ContainerSpec doesn't include the field — docker service inspect shows Image: <ref>@sha256:<pinned> with no pull_policy. Digest pins at deploy time; future webhook fires with same :latest don't re-resolve. New section in cicd-deployment.md splits the Permanent Fix per orchestrator: (1) plain Compose → pull_policy: always (unchanged from v4.6.1), (2) Swarm → three options (Portainer BE webhook with --resolve-image always, OR digest-pinned image via CI, OR SHA-tagged images), (3) Portainer UI Update + Re-pull works for both. Detection one-liner: docker info | grep 'Swarm:'. v4.6.1 codifies the Portainer-native deploy policy (caught during 2026-05-11 ProDevs-News field test on M1 Max). `references/cicd-deployment.md` gains a new "Deployment Recovery Policy (MANDATORY)" section: never `gh auth | ssh docker login + docker pull` as a deploy step (persists long-lived GHCR token on host, bypasses Portainer stack audit log, creates a second deploy path that diverges from canonical). Three Portainer-native recovery routes documented (UI re-pull-checkbox / webhook with pullImage=true / `gh run rerun`). Permanent fix is `pull_policy: always` per service — now shown in the example `portainer/stack-production.yml` with a callout comment. The `/deploy` command step 6 explicitly bans manual pull. Manual `gh auth | ssh docker login` is acceptable ONLY as a one-off diagnostic with mandatory `docker logout ghcr.io` cleanup. Battle-tested development discipline plugin. Enforces 11 engineering pillars via skills, agents, hooks, and commands. v4.6.0 polish wave + continuous-drive mode + user-direct-input detection. (H1) `launch_cc.sh` now opens a NEW Terminal/iTerm WINDOW (not a tab) when another terminal-mode CC is already running — prevents the watchdog from routing keystrokes to the wrong CC. (H2) `learning.sh` prints `[learning] event=<cat> ws=<id>` confirmation on stderr after every successful append, validates that all positional args are `key=value`, and rejects empty workspace / category. (F2) `launch_cc.sh --dry-run` prints what it WOULD spawn (workspace + flags + new-window-vs-tab decision) without doing anything. (F3) `state.sh tail <workspace> [N]` and `state.sh recent <workspace> [N]` pretty-print the last N JSONL events — no more `tail -N | jq` for users who don't know jq. (F4) Git pre-commit hook `check_no_hardcoded_paths.sh` scans staged files in `commands/skills/assets/agents/hooks/.claude-plugin/` for `/Users/<name>/` hardcodes and refuses the commit (with remediation hint) — would have prevented C5 entirely. Install via `bash develop-like-sudipta/hooks/scripts/install_precommit_path_check.sh`. (F5) `learning.sh` now reads stdin (when not a tty) into an optional `body` field — supports long-form notes / markdown / log excerpts that don't fit in kv pairs. (D1) Plugin layout diagram added to `/cc-drive`. (H3+new) Continuous-drive mode: both the `directive_template.md` (CC side) and `/cc-drive` doc (Cowork side) now have explicit "don't wait for pings" sections. CC keeps working through phase tasks without per-task confirmation; Cowork keeps polling without per-phase user confirmation. Three escalation triggers only: verify-gate red after 3 fix attempts, hard external blocker, user explicit stop. PLUS: user-direct-input detection — Cowork compares CC scrollback against the `message_sent` frags it logged in `state.json` and flags any user-typed input that bypassed Cowork, logging a `user_direct_input` state event and pausing one poll cycle to avoid duplicating CC's response. v4.5.1 fixes THREE critical bugs caught by field-testing on M1 Max (full feedback report attached during this session): (C2) `launch_cc.sh` and `start_watchdog.sh` were false-positive matching Cursor's IDE-agent claude binary under `~/.cursor/extensions/`. Promoted both to a shared `is_terminal_cc()` filter that excludes `Claude.app/Contents/`, `.cursor/extensions/*claude-code*`, AND any `--output-format stream-json` command, AND requires a real TTY (`ps -o tty=` not `??`). Real terminal CCs have ttys like `ttys003`. (C3) `send.sh` verify-by-fragment was false-negative on em-dashes and other Unicode characters above U+007E because pbcopy ⇄ osascript paste ⇄ Terminal scrollback re-encodes them, breaking literal byte-grep. Picker now grabs the longest ASCII-only run of ≥15 chars via `LC_ALL=C grep -oE '[!-~ ]{15,200}'` and slices from its middle. (C4) `diagnose.sh` died silently mid-run when an inner `osascript` call in `WIN=$(...)` returned non-zero (permission denied / no front window) — set -euo pipefail propagated the failure out of `$(...)`. Each inner osascript now has its own `|| echo "?"` fallback. v4.5 adds `/ccbridge-status` — a one-screen ground-truth view of the v4.3+ closed loop on this machine, with NO state mutations. The backing `ccbridge_status.sh` script is callable standalone (works from any shell — Cowork sandbox, Desktop_Commander, SSH, anywhere) and reports: plugin version + install dir, bridge install (script presence checked against canonical 22-name list including all v4.3.x + v4.4 additions, cache subdirs, registered project count from `~/.cache/ccbridge/projects.json`), watchdog process (status + PID + WORKSPACE env via `ps eww`), per-category event counts in last 7 days across all projects (in-memory Counter over `~/.cache/ccbridge/learnings/*.jsonl`), latest distillation report + cross-project signature count + last 3 lines of `.decisions.log`, best autoresearch score per skill (handles both JSON-array baselines.json and legacy JSONL format), and a one-word HEALTH verdict (`green` if no problems, `red` with problem count if anything missing — triggers a remediation hint to run `/ccbridge-init`). The slash command at `/ccbridge-status` (in `commands/`) wraps the shell script with a merge step that calls `mcp__scheduled-tasks__list_scheduled_tasks` and renders next-run/last-run times for the two ccbridge tasks + the autoresearch task. Pre-flight v5.0 work (continuous-monitoring `/cc-monitor` driver — observe browser + SSH logs, classify anomalies, fix-deploy via existing bug-driven TDD, heartbeat loop with `max_cycles` + `max_duration_hours` stop conditions). v4.4 adds CC auto-launch: new `launch_cc.sh` does detect-or-spawn for a SPECIFIC workspace. Detection scans `ps -axo pid=,command=` for terminal-mode `claude` binaries (filtering out Cowork-embedded Claude.app/ paths), then reads each candidate's cwd via `lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd` and matches against the requested workspace. If a CC is already running for THAT workspace → returns its PID, no spawn. If none → spawns a new Terminal.app (or iTerm2, honoring `TERMINAL_APP`) tab running `cd '<workspace>' && claude --continue --chrome` (flags configurable via `CC_LAUNCH_FLAGS` env OR per-project `.cc/config.json` → `cc_launch_flags`). Polls up to 30s (configurable via `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_S`) for the new claude PID to register with the matching cwd, then returns it. `--detect-only` flag for safe observability (exits 4 if no match, never spawns). Wired into `start_watchdog.sh` as a self-bootstrap step (when WORKSPACE is set, launch_cc runs first), so the watchdog can ensure CC exists before attaching. Verified `--chrome` and `--continue` against `claude --help` on this Mac. v4.3.4 fixes TWO real bugs caught on a second Mac during v4.3.3 rollout: (A) `setup_ccbridge.sh` exited cleanly at step 1 and never reached step 2 (SKILL copy) because `install.sh | sed 's/^/[install] /'` ran under `set -euo pipefail`, and a SIGPIPE inside install.sh's own pipeline (`diagnose.sh | head -25`) propagated upward, killing setup_ccbridge.sh silently with exit 0 from the user's perspective but no SKILLs copied. Fix: capture install.sh stdout to a tmpfile via mktemp + trap-cleanup, then `sed` over the file (no pipeline), so SIGPIPE inside install.sh can't break the outer flow. Defensive: also wrapped `diagnose.sh | head -25` in install.sh with `|| true`.
